chapter: Will Marion Cook and the Southern Syncopated Orchestra
title: After Oslo, forming a five-piece for Murray's Club
summary: After three months in Oslo the group folded in London, and Briggs formed a five-piece for Murray's Club with Salnave and the Gold Coast pianist Caleb Quaye (Mope Desmond), in clubs owned by Jack May.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Then, after the Hammersmith affair, I went to--wait a minute was it Oslo, yes, I went to Oslo, yes. 'Cause George Hines was still with us, we kept George Hines, it was the same group with this piano player that was imposed by the manager.
We went to Oslo for three months and after the three months we came back, we went back to London, and then the band, we folded then.

And I formed another orchestra, five pieces for the Murray's Club. We had two of the Syncopated Orchestra, and -- three of the Syncopated Orchestra, with Salnave, the flutist, who was then a saxophone player. He bought a saxophone, --
And we played at the Murray's Club. We had taken an African piano player by the name of Caleb Quaye, he called himself, Mope Desmond.
Mope Desmond and his real name was Caleb Quaye?

Q-u-a-y-e, Quaye. He was from the Gold Coast, I think.* He was a very fine piano player and a nice musician, because he came over to study music, and we worked at various clubs, who was owned, this is funny, by another American, Jack May.
And his secretary, Jack May's secretary's name was Mr. Cordell Hull.
My memory is pretty good. I didn't put down on paper, this is a long while, isn't it? And I just still remember.
wonderful engagement at this high spot, what you call a society spot, and we had two bands, there was another band, an English band.
